chunks: Abul-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', from Al-Khaybari, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari al-Qummi, who said:

Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Baghdad is like whoever visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), except that the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Believers have their own specific superiority. And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, through his chain, similarly.'

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Believers (Imam Ali)
key_terms.قَبْرَ أَبِي: The grave of my father (Imam Musa al-Kadim)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Musa al-Kadim in Baghdad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) elevates the spiritual merit of visiting Imam Musa al-Kadhim’s (a.s.) shrine in Baghdad to that of the Prophet and Imam Ali, emphasizing that while the reward is comparable, the intrinsic rank of the Prophet and Imam Ali remains superior. This hadith, recorded by Ibn Qulawayh, highlights the significance of Baghdad as a major center of Shia pilgrimage during the Abbasid era, reinforcing the concept of *ziyarah* as a means of connecting with the divine authority (*wilayah*) of the Imams.
